## Answer

Pro-rata amounts are **rounded to 2 decimal places, half-up**. [DOM-BILL-PRORATA-001@1.0.0 | active | high]

The rounding applies to the pro-rata amount for mid-cycle activations, which is calculated as (monthly fee / days in billing period) × remaining days. [DOM-BILL-PRORATA-001@1.0.0 | active | high] The billing period is always the calendar month. [DOM-BILL-PRORATA-001@1.0.0 | active | high]

There's also a note captured from the code, but it's not established knowledge yet. It points at `src/billing.js:12-14` (commit `abc1234`), which does `Math.round(amount * 100) / 100`. From that line it concludes the rounding is half-up *for positive amounts*. A search for `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in `src/` found nothing. [FRAG-BILL-ROUNDING-001@1.0.0 | ingested | low]

| FRAG-BILL-ROUNDING-001 | 1.0.0 | ingested | low | local | What the code was observed doing; not yet turned into a spec |

## Caveats
- **The spec doesn't say how to round negative amounts** (credits, refunds). The code note only covers positive amounts. That matters here: JavaScript's `Math.round` rounds a half toward positive infinity, so −0.5 becomes 0 rather than −1, which isn't symmetric half-up. Nothing in the specs says which behaviour is intended.
- The specs also don't say whether to round once at the end or at each step (e.g. the daily rate). They also don't mention floating-point precision, even though `amount * 100` can cause it to round wrong.
- The spec has no linked specs in the graph, so expanding it turned up nothing more.
- The code note hasn't been folded into a spec yet. Consolidating it with `/kdd:spec-consolidate` would be a good time to fill the gaps above.
